name: phd-bs-nd-double-count-cap
description: A Ph.D. student straight from Notre Dame's 4+1 track who never finished the MSCSE (no Notre Dame master's on record), with four senior-year 60000-level courses on the undergraduate side of the transcript. The Graduate School, through the DGS (2026-09-22): "Only up to 6 credits may double-count towards two degrees." Three courses the bachelor's degree used ('bs') would each count toward two degrees — the first two fit the six credits, the third is over the allowance and counts nothing; a course the bachelor's did not use ('neither') counts in full. The new phd.cap.sharedbs row reports the allowance. Nothing here is transfer credit. 2026-10-03 (policy review): the Academic Code’s §4.6 writes the six-credit exception for an integrated bachelor’s/MASTER’S program, so the bachelor’s + Ph.D. sharing rests on the Graduate School’s answer alone — the two counted courses are provisional until the DGS confirms, the allowance row waits for the DGS, and the review request asks.

detailIncludes: 6 of the 6 credits that may still count toward both your bachelor’s degree and the Ph.D. used
